rows.note: Built like for like rather than comparing revenue against FCF. Revenue 9,516,000,000 compounding at 6% for five years gives 12,733,700,000 in FY2030; at a 21% steady-state operating margin that is operating income of 2,674,077,000. Two cash-conversion readings are carried through, both computed from fundamentals.operating_cashflow_fy less capex_fy over operating_income_fy: holding FY2025's own ratio (0.6921) gives FY2030 free cash flow of 1,851,030,000, a 3.67% FCF CAGR from the 1,546,000,000 base; using the average of FY2023 (0.8081) and FY2025 (0.6921), excluding FY2024 (2.021, an outlier caused by that year's depressed 627,000,000 operating-income base rather than a real conversion improvement), gives 0.7501, FY2030 free cash flow of 2,005,894,000, and a 5.35% CAGR. Against the filed 5-year market-implied 11.37%, the gap is 5.82 to 7.70 percentage points, clearing the file's own 3.93-point horizon_spread: a real gap by the file's own rule. Against the filed 10-year market-implied 7.44%, the same builds are only 2.09 to 3.77 points behind, INSIDE the horizon_spread: not a claimable gap by the file's own percentage-point rule at that horizon. The direction does not flip between horizons (both say the market wants more than this dive defends), only the SIZE of the percentage-point finding does, and forward-solving the filed reverse-DCF's own bisection formula at this dive's own builds shows the PRICE gap survives even where the growth-rate gap does not: at g=3.67% the fair price is $217.04 at the 5-year convention and $226.96 at the 10-year convention (31.23% and 28.09% below the $315.61 reference); at the more generous g=5.35% build the fair price is $236.31 at 5 years and $263.32 even at 10 years (25.12% and 16.57% below reference). This dive claims the 5-year reading as the operative one, consistent with this analyst's prior VRT/HUBB/MYRG/ESLT dives choosing the tougher convention as the default read, while disclosing the 10-year reading in full rather than hiding it.

independence_test.largest_disagreement: The market's 5-year reverse-DCF convention asks an 11.37% FCF CAGR from a broker whose reported revenue actually fell 2.29% in FY2025 and whose trailing three-year CAGR is only 2.93%; even crediting the Newfront acquisition and the company's own guided mid-single-digit organic path in full, this dive's own like-for-like build defends only 3.67% to 5.35% (depending on which year's cash-conversion ratio is held), a gap of 5.8 to 7.7 percentage points that survives the file's own 3.93-point horizon-convention allowance at the 5-year reading and translates into a fair price 17% to 31% below the reference close even under the friendliest combination of assumptions tested.
independence_test.why_the_gap_exists: The category of error this dive identifies is a conflation of the ADJUSTED (non-GAAP) margin narrative with GAAP cash economics: WTW's own Propel plan and adjusted operating margin (19.5% Q2 2026, up 100bp) are the headline the market is reacting to, while GAAP operating margin is simultaneously falling (16.6% H1 2026 versus 17.8% H1 2025, 14.8% versus 16.3% for Q2 alone), the gap driven by Newfront-related transaction and integration expenses the adjusted figure excludes. Sell-side coverage (Moderate Buy, average target 369.38) reflects broad, longstanding WTW fundamentals research, not a Hormuz-specific catalyst: the chain's own heat block scores specialty-marine-broking crowdedness 30 (UNDISCOVERED) even though the issuer is PCS Axis B SATURATED (102.4% institutional ownership, 19 analysts), which argues professional investors know this NAME very well without having connected it to THIS occurrence specifically.
independence_test.falsification: Stated to prove this dive WRONG, not to confirm it. If nine-month 2026 consolidated organic revenue growth prints at or above 6% (above every quarterly organic print in the 2026 series so far and above the guided mid-single-digit path) AND nine-month 2026 GAAP operating margin recovers to or above 17.8% (matching H1 2025's own level, reversing this year's decline rather than merely slowing it), that combination would show the Propel-driven structural expansion is arriving in GAAP terms faster than this dive credits, which would narrow or close the residual gap and undercut the skepticism behind bear[0] and bear[1]. Two legs deliberately, because either one alone (strong growth with weak margin, or strong margin with weak growth) would leave the other half of this dive's disagreement with the market unaddressed.
